docs.title: Frappe Research Hub
docs.text:
Learn Frappe Framework and ERPNext from Noob to Pro — from first bench setup to production ERP. Guides, research, new apps, and real-world use cases, in one place.

By Muhammad Irfaan — Full-Stack Developer & ERP Specialist, NexTash, Lahore. Building ERP systems businesses actually rely on.

📖 Read it as a website: irfanzahoor.github.io/frappe-research-hub — search, navigation, dark mode. Same content as this repo.

docs.title: Choosing Apps — When to Install One vs Build It
docs.text: Every app you install is a dependency you will carry at every upgrade. An app that saves two days today and breaks the next upgrade costs two weeks. This guide is the decision process NexTash uses before any bench get-app — on a client project or on our own sites.

docs.title: The 5 questions — ask them before installing anything
docs.text:
No app gets installed until all five have an answer, in writing, on the project note:

  1. Does it solve a real problem on a real project? Not "it looks useful" — a named client, a named pain, this month. An app installed "for later" is a dependency with no owner.
  2. Is it maintained? Check the repo: a release in the last 6 months, open issues getting answers, stars as a rough signal only. A repo with no commit in a year is a dead app walking — you will be its maintainer.
  3. Does it match your Frappe / ERPNext version? It needs a branch for your version — version-14, version-15, version-16 — or a README that says so. "Works on v15" is not "works on v16".
  4. Does it have a migration path out? Can you export the data and uninstall cleanly? If removing it means losing the data or hand-editing the database, you do not own the data — the app does.
  5. Who owns it when it breaks? A named person, not "the team". If nobody owns it, it breaks on the client's busiest day and nobody knows whose job it is.

One "I don't know" is fine — test it on staging and find out. Two or more "I don't know" means do not install it yet.

docs.title: Install it — when someone else already solved it well
docs.text:
Install when the problem is a whole module, the app is official or well-maintained, and building it would take weeks:

Need Install Why CRM Frappe CRM — bench get-app https://github.com/frappe/crm Official, actively developed, web forms + pipeline. See CRM lesson. Support desk Frappe Helpdesk Official, SLAs + portal + knowledge base. See Helpdesk lesson. HR Frappe HRMS (hrms app) Official HR: leave, attendance, payroll. See HR lesson. Chat Raven (official, github.com/frappe/raven) Team chat inside Desk; v3 is the current version. POS POSNext (v15+, offline mode) or POS Prime (v14/v15/v16, zero core changes) A POS is a product, not a feature — never build one from scratch. Dashboards Frappe Insights Official BI on live data. Note: v3.50 removed v2 — migrate v2 dashboards first. WhatsApp Frappe WhatsApp Suite (+ chat UI + chatbot) or official WABA Integration The channel clients in Pakistan actually read.

Rule of thumb: if the app is official Frappe code, install it first and argue later. Official apps get version branches, upgrade patches and a migration path — the three things that cost you at upgrade time.

docs.title: Build it — when the gap is small and specific
docs.text:
Build when the need is one register, one form, one small workflow — not a whole module:

  • A gate-pass register, a sample tracker, a visitor log. A Studio mini-app, built visually in a day by an analyst (see Studio, Flow & Insights). Installing a whole app for one register is like hiring a company to fix a tap.
  • One extra field or one small rule on an existing DocType. A Custom Field (as a fixture) or a Server Script — not an app, not a fork. See Server Scripts.
  • A gap nobody has built for. Pakistan payments are the real example: there is no free public Easypaisa / JazzCash app — the catalog's biggest gap. That is a build (on Payment Core, github.com/aerele/payment-core), and it is a product opportunity, not just a project task.

If the build is under a day in Studio or a week in code, build it. If it is over a month, look for an app again — or charge the client for the build honestly, as a product, not a favour.

docs.title: Extend it — the middle path
docs.text:
Most real work is neither install nor build — it is extending what is already there, from your own app:

  • Custom Fields and Property Setters, exported as fixtures.
  • Server Scripts for one quick rule (see Server Scripts).
  • doc_events in hooks.py pointing at an override file in your app.
  • A whitelisted method + frappe.call for a button that does server work.

And the hard rule, always: never edit another app's code. Not one line, not "just this once". The next bench update wipes it, and the client finds out on a Monday. Extend from your app, or do not do it. (See Common mistakes §2.)

docs.title: Red flags — walk away
docs.text:
• Abandoned. Last commit over a year ago, issues unanswered. TailPOS (last activity Oct 2022) and ALYF Banking (repo flagged Archived) are the catalog's examples — staging test only, never promise them.
  • It forks core DocTypes. An app that replaces or rewrites Sales Order / Stock Entry will break on the next ERPNext update. Check what it overrides before you install it.
  • No version branch for your Frappe version. "Works on v15" on a v16 site is a staging-test failure waiting to happen.
  • It needs Administrator to work. An app that only functions as Administrator has a permission model of "everyone is admin". Do not put it on a client site.
  • Paid, with no trial. A price with no way to test on staging is a sales call, not a product. Ask for a staging licence first.
  • No uninstall story. If the README says nothing about removing it, assume the data is trapped.

docs.title: Worked example — one client, three needs
docs.text:
A spice manufacturer (the fmc demo client) asks for three things. Same framework, three different answers:

(a) CRM — install. Real problem (leads live in WhatsApp), official app (Frappe CRM, github.com/frappe/crm), version-16 branch, data exportable, owner: the sales lead. Decision: bench get-app Frappe CRM. Never start a client on the legacy ERPNext CRM — it is scheduled for removal in v17.

(b) Gate-pass register — build. One form, one list, one approval. No app in the catalog does just this, and a whole app for one register is a dependency with no payoff. Decision: build it in Studio in a day — form, list view, approval step — published to the Desktop. (This is the Studio example.)

(c) WhatsApp notifications — install. Real problem (customers never read email), maintained app, version branch exists. Decision: install the Frappe WhatsApp Suite (Business Cloud API + in-Desk chat + chatbot) — or the official WABA Integration if the client wants Frappe-maintained code only. Order and invoice alerts go out on document events; the chat UI replaces the shared phone the sales team passes around.

docs.title: Maintenance cost — every app is an upgrade dependency
docs.text: An installed app is not free after install day. At every upgrade, each app is one more branch to check, one more migrate that can fail, one more staging test. Before the next upgrade, list every installed app and ask the 5 questions again — an app that was right last year can be abandoned this year. The full upgrade process is in the Upgrade guide.

docs.text:

  • [ ] Repo checked: recent release, issues answered, version branch for your Frappe version
  • [ ] Uninstall + data export tested on staging first
  • [ ] An owner named for when it breaks
  • [ ] Installed on staging, tested with real user accounts (not Administrator)

docs.title: Common Mistakes — the ones real projects actually make
docs.text: Short, concrete, from real NexTash work. Each mistake has the fix. If you recognise your own project in any section, fix that one first.

docs.title: 1. Bad field layout
docs.text:
The mistake: a DocType with 20 fields stacked in one long column, no Section Breaks, no Column Breaks, and everything ticked "In List View". The form is a scroll nobody reads, and the list is 12 columns wide.

The fix — five rules:

  1. Read the form first. Open the existing form before adding a field. Add to the flow that is already there.
  2. Place with insert_after. Every new field names the field it goes after. Fields without a position land at the bottom in a pile.
  3. Two fields per row. Field, Column Break, field — then a Section Break starts the next row.
  4. A child table gets its own section. Section Break with a clear label ("Items") before it.
  5. Max 4–5 columns in List View. Only the fields a user scans to find a record.

Existing forms with bad layout are left as-is — these rules apply to fields created going forward, not to rebuilding old forms.

docs.title: 2. Hooks in the wrong place
docs.text:
The mistake: business logic written inside hooks.py, doc_events for a DocType your own app owns, or a "*" doc_event that runs on every save of every DocType. Or worse: editing ERPNext's files directly to change a behaviour.

The fix — the placement rules:

What Where it goes Logic on your own DocType Its controller (validate, on_submit, …) Logic on another app's DocType doc_events in hooks.py → an override file in your app Form JS for another app's DocType public/js/<name>.js + doctype_js in hooks.py Custom Field / Property Setter Fixtures, filtered by module

And the hard rules:

  • hooks.py is a registry, not a code file. Only dotted paths, no logic.
  • Never edit another app's files. Not even "one small line". Extend from your app, or the next update wipes it.
  • Never "*" doc_events unless the logic truly applies to every DocType — it runs on every save, everywhere, forever.
  • No duplicate frappe.ui.form.on blocks for the same DocType — extend the existing handler.
  • Validation on the server. JS is UX only. A rule enforced in JS alone is not a rule — the API bypasses it.
# hooks.py — registry only
doc_events = {
    "Sales Invoice": {
        "validate": "my_app.selling.overrides.sales_invoice.validate",
    },
}

docs.title: 3. Permission mistakes
docs.text:
The mistake: users who cannot see their own documents, or users who can see everything. Both are usually the same three errors.

The fix:

  • Hiding a field in JS is not security. Anyone can read the field through the API. Use permlevel (field-level permission) instead.
  • ignore_permissions=True without a reason. If you pass it, write the reason in a comment next to it. Otherwise the next developer copies it everywhere.
  • allow_guest=True on anything that writes. Guest endpoints are read-only, rate-limited, and must validate every input.
  • v16: has_permission must return an explicit True. Returning None now denies access (on v14/v15, None meant "no opinion"). A hook that forgets to return True locks everyone out.
  • Sharing is not a role. Sharing one document gives access to that one document only — the user still needs read permission on the DocType. A user who sees an empty list usually has a User Permission (Company, Branch) hiding the documents, not a missing share.
  • Whitelisted methods check permission first. Check with frappe.has_permission(..., throw=True) before returning data, not after. A method without @frappe.whitelist() cannot be called from a form or the API at all (403).

403? Check in this order: role permission on the DocType → User Permission hiding the document → has_permission hook returning None or False → whitelisted method missing the decorator or the check → the API token's user lacking the role.

docs.title: 4. Performance mistakes
docs.text:
The mistake: a report or a submit that takes 30 seconds, usually for one of four reasons.

The fix:

N+1 queries — the big one. Never frappe.get_doc inside a loop to read one value.

# ❌ one query per row
for row in self.items:
    group = frappe.db.get_value("Item", row.item_code, "item_group")

# ✅ one query, then a dict lookup
item_codes = [row.item_code for row in self.items]
groups = dict(frappe.get_all("Item",
    filters={"name": ("in", item_codes)},
    fields=["name", "item_group"], as_list=True))
for row in self.items:
    group = groups.get(row.item_code)
  • Use the right read. frappe.db.get_value / frappe.get_cached_value for one field — not get_doc. Aggregates in SQL, not by loading rows into Python.
  • Add search_index on fields used in frequent filters.
  • Never frappe.db.commit() inside a request. The framework commits. (Allowed only in long background jobs / patches, in batches.)
  • Slow work goes to a background job. Anything over a few seconds — bulk processing, bulk email, external APIs, big reports — goes through frappe.enqueue(..., queue="long"), and the user is notified on completion.
  • Do not call the server from refresh for data that rarely changes. Load once in onload, or set frm.doc.__onload from the controller.

docs.title: 5. Ledger and stock — the unforgivable ones
docs.text:
• Never insert GL Entry or Stock Ledger Entry directly. They are created automatically on submit. If a posting is missing, the document is wrong — fix the document.
  • Never edit a submitted document's fields. Cancel and amend. An edited submitted document and its ledger disagree forever.
  • Never edit Bin by hand. Wrong balance? Stock Reconciliation, with a posting date and a reason.

docs.title: Pre-ship checklist
docs.text:
Before any custom app goes to a client, check:

  • [ ] Every new field placed with insert_after, 2 per row, child tables in their own section, ≤ 5 list columns
  • [ ] No logic in hooks.py; no "*" doc_events; no edits to other apps
  • [ ] Validation on the server, not only in JS
  • [ ] No ignore_permissions=True without a comment; no allow_guest writes
  • [ ] No get_doc in a loop; slow work enqueued
  • [ ] No hand-written GL / SLE rows; no edits to submitted documents
  • [ ] bench --site <site> migrate run, and a backup taken before it

docs.title: Go-Live Checklist
docs.text: Go-live is a project, not a day. The system is ready when the data is right, the users can do their jobs, and the old system can still save you. A distributor went live with perfect code and wrong opening stock — the first month's reports were fiction. This checklist exists so that does not happen again.

docs.title: 1. Data import order
docs.text:
Import in dependency order — a transaction cannot reference a master that does not exist yet:

1. Company → Chart of Accounts → Cost Centers → Tax Templates
2. Masters: Item (+ Item Group, UOM, Warehouse), Customer, Supplier,
   Price List, BOM
3. Opening balances: stock + accounts (section 2)
4. Open transactions: open Sales Orders, Purchase Orders, open
   Sales/Purchase Invoices, open Payment Entries

Rules: one file per DocType, imported with Data Import (v16.50 has a step-based wizard — use it). Validate on a test import first; never import straight into live. Reconcile every import: row counts in the file vs rows in the system, ten records opened by hand. Bad data is fixed in the file and re-imported — the file is the record.

docs.title: 2. Opening balances
docs.text:
Stock — Stock Reconciliation, posting date = the cutover date, with a reason on every line. Bin quantities must match the physical count. If the warehouse count and the sheet disagree, the count wins and the difference is written down, not hidden.

Accounts — customer and supplier opening balances through the Opening Invoice Creation Tool (one opening invoice per party, dated the cutover date), bank and cash opening through Journal Entry. Then the test that matters: Trial Balance must balance (debits = credits) before go-live. If it does not balance, go-live waits.

Reconcile before the users arrive: stock value in the books vs the stock report, Accounts Receivable vs the customer ledger, Accounts Payable vs the supplier ledger. Three numbers, three matches, no exceptions.

docs.title: 3. Permissions & roles
docs.text:
• Roles and permissions set in Role Permission Manager — per DocType, per role, not per person. User Permissions (Company, Warehouse, Branch) for users who must see only their own branch or warehouse.
  • Test with real user accounts. Log in as the accountant, the store keeper, the sales rep — and do their actual job: create a Sales Invoice, submit a Stock Entry, approve a Purchase Order. Testing as Administrator proves nothing; Administrator can do everything.
  • Portal users (customers, suppliers) tested too — they log in through the portal and see only their own documents.
  • On v16, has_permission hooks must return an explicit True (see Lesson 09). A hook returning None locks everyone out.
  • Hiding a field in JS is not security — use permlevel. Validation on the server, not only in JS (see Common mistakes).

docs.title: 4. User training
docs.text:
• NexTash trains the client's super users; super users train their teams. Training the whole staff directly does not scale and does not stick.
  • Material per role, one page per job: "How to make a Sales Invoice", "How to receive stock", "How to approve a leave application". Short SOPs, not a manual nobody reads.
  • Training happens on a training site with sample data, never on live. Users break things in training and learn; users break things in live and the business stops.
  • Every role does its real work once in training — the first real invoice should not be the first invoice ever made.

docs.title: 5. Cutover plan
docs.text:
• Freeze date agreed in writing. No new transactions in the old system after Friday close. Anything after the freeze goes into ERPNext.
  • Final import on Saturday: masters delta (customers or items added during the week), opening balances, open transactions.
  • Delta entries: anything that slipped through after the final import is entered by hand on Monday morning and ticked off a list.
  • Communication: every user knows the freeze date, the go-live date, and who to call when stuck. The client's manager announces it.

docs.title: 6. Backups & restore test
docs.text:
bench --site <site> backup --with-files
  • Scheduled backups on before go-live (on v16, offsite backups are a separate app — install it, do not assume it is built in).
  • Restore tested on a spare site before go-live. A backup that was never restored is not a backup.
  • Backup files kept off the server — a backup on the same disk as the database is a copy, not a backup.

docs.title: 7. Monitoring
docs.text: Week 1, someone checks daily: Scheduler running — bench doctor and the Background Jobs list in Desk. A stopped scheduler means no emails, no notifications, no auto-reposts — silently. Email Queue draining — emails sent, not stuck. Error Log clean — every error read, not just counted; one error repeated 200 times is one bug, fix it. Disk space — a full disk stops the database. Integrations end-to-end — payment gateway, WhatsApp, webhooks: one real transaction each, on go-live day.

docs.title: 8. Rollback / Plan B
docs.text:
• The old system stays runnable for one week. Excel, the old ERP, the paper register — whatever it was, it is not deleted on go-live day.
  • The rollback trigger is agreed in advance: e.g. "if invoicing is down for two hours, we revert to the old system and re-plan." Decided calmly now, not in a panic on Monday.
  • Data entered in ERPNext before a rollback must be exportable — know how to get it out (report export) before you need it.

docs.title: 9. Go-live day runbook
docs.text: Time Action Owner 08:00 Scheduler, Email Queue, Error Log, disk checked; backup taken NexTash 08:30 Users log in; each role opens its own workspace Super users 09:00 First real Sales Invoice made together with the sales team Sales super user 10:00 First stock movement checked against Bin Store keeper 12:00 First Payment Entry, bank balance checked Accountant 14:00 Error Log reviewed; any error fixed or logged with an owner NexTash 16:00 Day-1 sign-off call: what worked, what is blocked, tomorrow's list Client manager + NexTash 17:00 Backup taken; day-1 notes written down NexTash

docs.title: Go-live checklist
docs.text:
Data - [ ] Masters imported in order, row counts reconciled - [ ] Opening stock reconciled to physical count - [ ] Opening balances imported; Trial Balance balances - [ ] AR / AP / stock value reconciled to the ledgers - [ ] Open transactions imported (orders, open invoices)

Permissions - [ ] Roles set per DocType; User Permissions per branch/warehouse - [ ] Tested with real user accounts, not Administrator - [ ] Portal users tested

Training - [ ] Super users trained; SOPs per role written - [ ] Every role did its real work once on the training site

Cutover - [ ] Freeze date agreed in writing; final import done - [ ] Delta list ready for Monday morning

Backups & monitoring - [ ] Scheduled backups on; restore tested on a spare site - [ ] Scheduler, Email Queue, Error Log checked; integrations tested end-to-end

Rollback - [ ] Old system runnable for one week - [ ] Rollback trigger agreed with the client

docs.title: Upgrade Guide — v14 → v15 → v16
docs.text: Upgrades are projects, not commands. Every rule below comes from an upgrade that went wrong — usually because someone ran it straight on production.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
1. One major version at a time. v14 → v15, verify, then v15 → v16. Never skip v15 — v16 patches assume v15 schema is already in place.
  2. Staging first, always. The full upgrade runs on a copy of production data.
  3. A backup that was never restored is not a backup. Test the restore on staging first.
  4. Every custom app needs a branch for the target version — or it is removed first.

docs.title: 1. Readiness check
docs.text:
Establish what you are upgrading from — the source of truth, not memory:

grep __version__ apps/frappe/frappe/__init__.py apps/erpnext/erpnext/__init__.py
bench version

Then run the upgrade scan from frappe_core_skills (/frappe-upgrade-check): it searches your apps for every removed or changed API in the tables below and lists the files. Fix the hits first — found on staging it is a delay, on production an outage.

Runtime floor for the target version (from the frappe-upgrade skill): v15 needs Python 3.10–3.11 and Node 18/20; v16 needs Python 3.14+ (older versions fail with SyntaxError) and Node 24+. MariaDB 10.6+ on both; Ubuntu 24.04 recommended for v16.

Also list, on paper, before you start: every custom app, Server Script, Workflow, print format and integration (payment gateway, WhatsApp, email). Each one can break, and each needs an owner.

docs.title: 2. Backup — and prove it restores
docs.text:
bench --site <site> backup --with-files --compress

Then restore that backup onto the staging site and confirm the site opens and a document can be created. Take a server snapshot too (VM snapshot, or a Frappe Cloud backup), and keep the backup files until at least a week after the upgrade — deleting them on upgrade day is how a bad upgrade becomes a disaster.

bench --site staging restore <backup.sql> --with-public-files <public.tar> --with-private-files <private.tar>

docs.title: 3. Upgrade order
docs.text:
Framework first, then ERPNext, then the separate apps, then your custom apps. The branches are switched together, in dependency order:

cd ~/frappe-bench
bench switch-to-branch version-15 frappe erpnext hrms  # v14 -> v15
bench --site <site> migrate
bench switch-to-branch version-16 frappe erpnext hrms  # v15 -> v16
bench --site <site> migrate

bench migrate runs the patches for every app in dependency order. HRMS, Frappe CRM, Helpdesk and Payments are separate apps — each needs its own version-15 / version-16 branch. A custom app with no branch is removed before migrating, not after it fails.

On Frappe Cloud there are no bench commands — the version is switched in the site dashboard — but the rules are the same. After the jump, monthly patches come through bench update (v16.61.0 and friends are monthly now — see history).

docs.title: 4. Breaking changes — v14 → v15
docs.text:
The hits the upgrade scan finds most often:

Old / removed Use frappe.db.set() doc.db_set() frappe.db.update() frappe.db.set_value() frappe.db.set_value() on Singles frappe.db.set_single_value() frappe.db.set_temp / get_temp frappe.cache JS window.get_today / show_alert / user / roles frappe.datetime.get_today, frappe.show_alert, frappe.session.user, frappe.user_roles this in Client Scripts frm / cur_frm

Also: Server Scripts are disabled by default on v15+ — re-enable with bench set-config -g server_script_enabled 1. Event Streaming moved to its own app, and the frontend is Vue 3 — custom Vue 2 components need a rewrite; check on staging, not live.

docs.title: 5. Breaking changes — v15 → v16
docs.text:
Change Action has_permission hooks Must return an explicit True — returning None now denies access DB commit inside document hooks Not allowed — the framework commits Default list sort creation (was modified) — pass order_by explicitly where order matters frappe.get_doc(dt, name, field=val) No longer sets values frappe.sendmail(now=True) No longer commits State-changing API methods POST only (logout, upload_file, send_login_link) PDF Chrome renderer — wkhtmltopdf is deprecated, removed in v17 Classic print formats Deprecated — they stop working in v17, rebuild on the new print designer now /app URL /desk — fix bookmarks and hardcoded links Blog, Newsletter, Energy Points, Offsite backups Separate apps (offsite backups: frappe/offsite_backups)

Two app moves to plan, not discover: legacy ERPNext CRM is scheduled for removal in v17 — move the client to the Frappe CRM app now, during the v16 upgrade. And standard workspace customisations reset on upgrade — keep them in your own app as fixtures, never Desk edits.

docs.title: 6. Patches — and a failed patch
docs.text:
Schema and data changes live in patches/ with an entry in patches.txt — one patch per change, idempotent where possible. Patches that must never be skipped are listed in hooks.py as never_skip_patches = ["my_app.patches.v16_0.critical_data_fix"].

If a patch fails, migration stops. Read the traceback — it names the patch and the row. Fix the data on staging (a bad value, a duplicate, a missing master), not the patch. Never hand-edit the database to fake a patch as done — the next migrate trusts that lie. Re-run bench --site <site> migrate; it resumes from the failed patch. bench migrate --skip-failing is for non-critical failures only — a skipped patch is a debt entry, not a success.

A spice-factory client once had a patch fail on a duplicate batch number. The fix was merging the duplicates on staging, then re-running migrate — ten minutes. Skipping the patch would have left two batches with one number in production stock.

docs.title: 7. Test the upgrade on the staging copy
docs.text:
Restore the production backup to staging, run the whole upgrade there, then test — by hand, not by hope: Desk loads and /desk works; for every DocType the upgrade touched, create, save, submit, cancel, print, and one list-view filter; run the app tests with bench --site <test_site> run-tests --app <app>; re-check every whitelisted method, workflow and scheduled job; open the client's real invoice on the Chrome renderer. Only when staging passes does production get a date.

Rollback plan: if migrate fails halfway, restore the pre-upgrade backup onto the old code (git checkout the old branches, restore DB + files). If you cannot do that in under an hour on staging, you are not ready to upgrade production. Agree it with the client beforehand: "if migrate fails and cannot be fixed in two hours, we restore."

docs.title: 8. Checklists
docs.text:
Before the upgrade:

  • [ ] Current versions recorded; upgrade scan run, hits fixed
  • [ ] Runtime meets the target version (Python, Node, MariaDB, OS)
  • [ ] Backup taken with --with-files --compress, restore tested
  • [ ] Every app has a branch for the target version (or is removed)
  • [ ] Server Scripts, workflows, print formats, integrations listed, each with an owner
  • [ ] Full upgrade rehearsed on a staging copy of production data
  • [ ] Staging tests pass (create/save/submit/cancel/print, run-tests)
  • [ ] Rollback plan agreed with the client, restore rehearsed

After the upgrade:

  • [ ] Desk loads, /desk URL, workspaces correct
  • [ ] Reports open (General Ledger, Stock Balance, Trial Balance)
  • [ ] Print formats render on Chrome PDF — real invoice checked
  • [ ] Scheduled jobs running (Scheduler, Background Jobs)
  • [ ] Email Queue draining, email sending works
  • [ ] Integrations tested end-to-end (payment gateway, WhatsApp, webhooks)
  • [ ] Permissions: has_permission hooks return True, roles tested with real users, not Administrator
  • [ ] Dashboards: upgraded sites keep classic dashboards until changed — switch to Insights only after checking each one
  • [ ] Offsite backups app installed (v16 — no longer built in)
  • [ ] Backup taken after the upgrade
